questions.q: In Overlook's pipeline, what are the source and sink for the Copy activity?
options: Source: OverlookDB, Sink: the scheduling system
Source: a PowerShell script, Sink: an email alert
Source: the failover group, Sink: Azure Monitor
Source: the scheduling system's export file in Azure Blob Storage, Sink: the dbo.Appointments table in OverlookDB
questions.explain: The daily export file is the source; the Appointments table in OverlookDB is the destination the Copy activity writes to.

questions.q: What are the three steps the Copy activity performs every single time, regardless of source or sink?
options: Encrypt, mask, audit
Backup, restore, verify
Read from the source, perform serialization/compression/column mapping, write to the sink
Provision, secure, monitor
questions.explain: This three-step process is the same underlying mechanism regardless of what specific source or sink is configured.

questions.q: Why does this pipeline only need the Azure Integration Runtime, not a self-hosted one?
options: Because both the source (Blob Storage) and the sink (Azure SQL) are publicly accessible cloud stores, reachable from Data Factory's own managed runtime
Self-hosted integration runtimes don't exist in Data Factory
Because the pipeline runs manually, not on a schedule
Because OverlookDB is on-premises
questions.explain: A self-hosted integration runtime is only needed when a source or sink sits behind an on-premises network — not the case for this pipeline's current setup.

questions.q: What does this lesson say the Copy activity is deliberately limited at, and where does heavier transformation belong instead?
options: It can't move any data at all without a mapping data flow
It's deliberately limited on heavy transformation (the "T" in ETL) — that belongs to a mapping data flow or an external compute engine, which this capstone's modest feed doesn't actually need
It requires a self-hosted integration runtime for any transformation
It can only read data, never write it
questions.explain: The Copy activity handles extract and load well, with light mapping/type conversion — not heavy transformation logic.

questions.q: What caution does this lesson give about the Copy activity's 'auto create table' feature for dbo.Appointments?
options: It replaces the need for any pipeline monitoring
It's useful for a first draft, but the auto-generated schema should be reviewed against the real schema the capstone actually needs before trusting it in production
It should never be used under any circumstances
It automatically applies TDE encryption
questions.explain: Auto-detected types from a source file don't always match what you'd design by hand — the same caution any auto-generated schema deserves.
